summary: Persona editor is the Workbench {{user}} sheet that reuses the character editor chassis: the three-column grid, BentoCard tiles, and portrait face plate. PortraitCard writes the persona portrait and KnowledgeRail manages knowledgeRefs. Identity contains the tagline, pronouns, brief, section tiles, and flat Identity Text. The right column has shared color controls, prompt-injection stops selected by the Write-for profile, a preview from core/persona/inject.ts, and the default-persona star. The compiler contract keeps brief out of injected content and prevents content from becoming the card blurb. The page records the component-catalog reuse rule and describes the Library persona shelf. Its Wires section covers rcpersona, RoleCall's V2 persona export, SillyTavern persona backups, Lumiverse, Marinara, and the absence of a standalone Agnai persona file wire. For SillyTavern backups, Bunzai imports the default persona and retains the other personas' field values for export; this is semantic value preservation, not byte-identical output.

sections.title: Reuse law on this surface
sections.summary: Every element on the persona editor was walked against the component catalog. Anything new on this surface must come from docs/reference/components.md first before inventing a twin control. The law matches house UI reuse: scan the generated catalog and share chassis pieces already used by character and regex editors such as WriteForStrip BentoCard and KnowledgeRail.

sections.title: The shelf
sections.summary: Library persona shelf lives in persona-shelf.tsx and persona-shelf-ops.ts. Cards show portrait or monogram, put the brief as the card line which is its one honest home, and surface pronouns section count and lorebook facts from the meta loader. A gilt Default badge marks the studio default persona preference.

sections.title: The wires
sections.summary: Supported persona wires include rcpersona and RoleCall's V2 side-channel export; SillyTavern persona backups; Lumiverse account objects with pronoun triplet data; and Marinara personas whose theming and stat bars remain in escrow. For a SillyTavern backup, Bunzai imports the default persona and retains the other personas' field values for export; serialized output is not promised to be byte-identical. Codec headers document detection firewalls. Agnai has no standalone persona file wire and uses the structured-persona component on character cards.
